title: Using Large Language Models to Create AI Personas for Replication, Generalization and Prediction of Media Effects: An Empirical Test of 133 Published Experimental Research Findings

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the replication success rates of 133 published experimental findings to observe how replicability declines with higher p-values and smaller effect sizes, as well as comparing the lower replication rates of interaction effects versus main effects.

Testing the generalizability of original human study results by running replications with varied AI persona profiles (e.g., modifying age to represent Gen Z vs. Seniors, altering geographic locations, and varying domain expertise) to uncover boundary conditions obscured by narrow human sampling.

Substituting original experimental media stimuli with alternative variations (e.g., different product categories or varied advertising imagery) to test if the published effects were artificially bound to the specific, narrow stimuli used in the original research.
